extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in travel, social observation, and 19th-century Mexico
extracted.subtask_description: A first‑person travel narrative reporting on cities, institutions, industry, and social conditions in 19th‑century Mexico, mixing descriptive observation with social and political commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press coverage focus (normative)
rubrics_metrics.description: The press too often reduces itself to personalities and party passions instead of addressing the real interests of the country (commerce, agriculture, industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author contrasts local newspapers that print 'autant de poésie que de prose' and dwell on personal attacks with American papers that report concrete economic information: what the mines produce, what the crop prospects are, duties collected, land prices and yields, machinery and new inventions. Implicit recommendation: newspaper coverage should prioritize substantive reporting on economic/industrial matters rather than partisan personalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational spending and priorities (observational/normative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary education reach versus cost and yield of secondary/higher education: the state supports many primary schools but still leaves a large uneducated population; secondary and higher schools are expensive and produce few professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites statistics: 433 primary schools instructing 17,211 children while 176,411 remain without instruction; costly secondary/superior schools produce few doctors, lawyers, engineers and each graduate costs thousands of piastres. Implicit guidance: prioritize broader primary education access and consider shifting some burdens from costly state provision to charity/ private initiative when appropriate; be mindful of per‑graduate costs when evaluating higher education investments.
